transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hey, yeah, nice to meet you too. Um, so I guess I'm here because I just keep making these really dumb mistakes at work. I supervise a sales team, and I have to do all these sales reports, and lately I just keep messing them up. Like, I'll copy the exact wrong numbers from the team dashboard, or I'll completely miss a line in a procedure I'm supposed to check. 

Which is crazy because the dashboard software we use is supposed to make it idiot-proof. We actually just switched to this new system right before Thanksgiving... I remember because my brother-in-law was over for dinner and he was bragging about how his company uses some fancy custom software. He's in logistics, totally different ballgame. He drives one of those massive rigs, which honestly sounds kind of nice sometimes, you know? Just being out on the open road instead of staring at a screen all day. I bought a motorcycle a few years ago thinking I'd do that on weekends, get out of the house, but it mostly just sits in the garage now. Need to get the battery replaced. 

But, uh, anyway, yeah... even when I swear I went over the reports and double-checked everything, I still somehow miss things and put the wrong numbers in. It's getting pretty embarrassing.
Did you have similar trouble paying attention or making careless mistakes when you were a kid in school?

Yeah, actually. I mean, my mom still brings it up sometimes. She kept all these old report cards and notes from my teachers in elementary school. They always said the same thing, like, I rushed through my work, or I was constantly losing my homework. Which is funny because my son, he's in fourth grade now, and he just lost his math workbook last week. We tore the house apart looking for it. Found it under the couch cushions, covered in dog hair. We have a Golden Retriever, Bailey, and she sheds like crazy. You can't wear black in our house, I swear. 

But yeah, the teacher notes... they also said I talked out of turn a lot and couldn't stay in my seat. They were always having to remind me to sit down. Kind of like now, I guess, just pacing around my office when I'm on phone calls.
Outside of work, do these attention problems also cause trouble at home or in other parts of your life?

Yeah, it definitely spills over. Like, at work, it's gotten bad enough that my manager actually put it in my formal review this year. Which was a huge bummer because I was hoping for a bump in pay to help with the kitchen remodel we're trying to do. We're putting in this farmhouse sink, you know, the big deep ones? My wife saw it on one of those home renovation shows, the one with the couple in Texas. They always use shiplap. I'm not totally sold on the shiplap, but the sink is nice. We had to order it special, took six weeks to get here. 

But anyway, yeah, at home it causes a lot of arguments too. It just adds to the conflict because my wife, and I guess my friends too, they feel like they just can't count on me to follow through on things. Like I'll say I'm going to do something and then I just... don't. Or I forget. Like I was supposed to pick up the dry cleaning on Tuesday and totally blew past the place. They close at six, which is so early, right? Who can get there by six?
When you're in a meeting or reading something important, do you find your mind drifting off even when you're trying to focus?

Yeah, all the time. It's like, I'll be sitting there trying to review my team's call notes or looking at the numbers for the week, and just one conversation across the room completely derails me. Or I'll get a random thought about something at home, like whether I remembered to close the garage door. We had a raccoon get in there once because I left it open. It got into the trash cans and made a huge mess. It took me all Sunday morning to clean it up, and my wife was so mad because we were supposed to go to her parents' house for brunch. Her mom makes these incredible blueberry pancakes, she uses actual buttermilk, which I guess makes a huge difference. I tried making them once from a mix and they just weren't the same. But yeah, anyway, it's like my mind just gets pulled off track before I even realize I've stopped reading. I'll get to the bottom of a page and have no idea what it actually said.
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to stay seated when you’re expected to?

Yeah, constantly. It's actually really uncomfortable. Like, if I'm sitting through a long meeting, it feels like my whole body is just buzzing inside. I end up having to shift around in my chair, or I'm tapping my foot the whole time. Sometimes I just have to make up an excuse to go to the bathroom or grab water just so I can stand up. The coffee machine at work is actually broken right now, which is a nightmare. It's one of those Keurig ones, and I think someone tried to use a pod that wasn't compatible and jammed the whole thing up. Now we have to walk all the way down to the lobby cafe if we want coffee, and they charge like five dollars for a regular drip. It's ridiculous. I should probably just start bringing a thermos from home, but I never remember to make it in the morning. I bought this really nice Yeti tumbler, the dark blue one, specifically for that. Keeps it hot for hours. But yeah, I just can't sit still for very long without feeling like I need to jump out of my skin.
Do these focus problems happen pretty much every day?

Yeah, pretty much every single day. It's just a constant thing. Like yesterday, I was trying to get through this stack of performance reviews for my team, and I just couldn't keep my eyes on the screen. Which is bad, because I really need to get them done before Friday. We're having this big team lunch on Friday at this new Italian place that opened up down the street. Supposedly they make all their pasta from scratch right there in the window. My buddy Dave went last week and said the lasagna was unbelievable, but he said parking is a total nightmare. You have to park like three blocks away and walk, which I don't mind, but you know how it is when you only have an hour for lunch. Plus, it's supposed to rain on Friday, so walking three blocks in the rain just for some lasagna seems like a lot of effort. I might just order a sandwich from the deli instead. They do this turkey club that's really good, they use that thick-cut bacon. But yeah, to answer your question, it's definitely an everyday struggle for me.
Do you often have trouble organizing tasks and activities?

Yeah, organization is... well, honestly, I don't really know if I have trouble with it or not. I mean, my desk at work is pretty messy, but I usually know where things are, mostly. It's like organized chaos, you know? My boss hates it. He's one of those guys who needs everything completely spotless. He actually came in on a Saturday once just to reorganize the supply closet because he couldn't stand how the printer paper was stacked. He's a good guy, though. He let me leave early a couple of weeks ago when my car broke down. The alternator just completely died on me right on the highway. I had to get it towed to this shop near my house, and the guy there tried to charge me like eight hundred bucks. I told him he was crazy, you can get a remanufactured one online for like a hundred and fifty. My brother-in-law is a mechanic, so I usually just have him look at stuff, but he was out of town on a fishing trip. They go up to this lake in Wisconsin every year for walleye. He caught a huge one last time, mounted it in his basement. His wife hates it, says it smells, but I think it looks pretty cool. But yeah, organization... I'm not really sure if it's a huge problem for me or just how I do things.
Have these attention problems caused serious problems in your life, like at work or in your relationships?

Yeah, it definitely has. It's actually gotten to the point where my manager put it in my formal review, which was really stressful. We had the review in that little glass conference room near the breakroom, the one where the AC is always blasting. I swear it's like forty degrees in there. I had to wear my heavy winter coat inside just to stop shivering. It's this North Face jacket I got on sale last Black Friday, actually a really good deal. I stood in line for like three hours outside the mall, which was crazy because it was snowing, but they were giving out those free hot chocolates from the kiosk, so it wasn't too bad. But yeah, the review was rough. And at home, it's causing issues too, because people feel like they can't count on me to follow through on things. It just adds to the conflict, you know? Like my sister was supposed to come over for dinner on Sunday, and she got all mad because she said I always forget to pick up the stuff she likes. She's doing this keto diet right now, which seems impossible to me. She's eating like, blocks of cheese and bacon, but no bread. I couldn't live without bread. There's this bakery near my house that makes these fresh sourdough loaves on weekend mornings, and the smell is just incredible. But yeah, it's definitely causing some real problems for me.
Do you often have trouble staying focused during things you do for fun, like watching a movie or reading at home?

I mean, I don't really know if I have trouble focusing on fun stuff. I guess it depends on what it is. Like, if I'm watching a movie, sometimes I'll pull out my phone and start scrolling, but everyone does that now, right? My wife and I were trying to watch that new superhero movie on streaming the other night, the one with the guy from that old sitcom. He looks so different now, I think he got hair plugs or something. Which is fine, no judgment, but it just looks a little unnatural around the hairline, you know? Anyway, we were watching it, and the dog started whining to go out. We have this golden retriever mix, Buster, and he's got this stomach thing where he can only eat this super expensive prescription food. We tried switching him to a cheaper brand once, and it was a disaster. I had to rent one of those carpet cleaners from the grocery store. Have you ever used one of those? They're incredibly heavy, and getting it into the trunk of my sedan was a whole workout. I really need to get an SUV, especially with winter coming. My buddy just bought a used Tahoe and he loves it, says it handles the snow like a champ. But yeah, for fun stuff... I don't know, I guess I haven't really paid attention to whether I lose focus or not.
Before age 12, did these attention or restlessness problems show up in more than one place, like both at school and at home?

Yeah, I was definitely like this as a kid, too. My mom actually still brings it up. She kept all these old report cards and notes from my teachers in elementary school, and they all said the same thing—that I'd rush through my work, lose my homework, talk out of turn, and just couldn't stay in my seat without them constantly reminding me. She keeps them in this giant plastic tub in her basement, right next to her sewing machine. She's super into quilting right now. It's wild, she spends hours matching up these tiny little squares of fabric. She made me this huge quilt for my bed last Christmas, all in these dark blue and gray colors. It's really warm, actually, maybe a little too warm. I had to kick it off the bed in the middle of the night last week because I woke up sweating. I usually sleep with a fan on, even in the winter, just for the white noise. I bought this tower fan from Costco a few years ago, and it has this little remote control that I always lose in the couch cushions. Our couch is one of those deep, squishy sectionals, and it just eats everything. I found like three dollars in quarters and a dog toy down there the other day. But yeah, the stuff at school and home... it's been happening since I was little, for sure.

Confirmed inattentive features include careless mistakes, distractibility, losing homework/items, forgetting obligations, and difficulty sustaining attention while reading or in meetings. Hyperactive/restless features include talking out of turn as a child, inability to stay seated, pacing, foot tapping, and internal restlessness. This is most consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation in ICD-10 coding as F90.0.
